### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, all 200 traces contained the same fixed fragment: A22 was followed directly by A23 in every observed case, and A23 directly by A24; A23 sat exactly one event after A22 and A24 exactly two events after A22. A14, A15 and A20 were not observed in any earlier trace. [DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG002, POS001, POS002, POS003, REL001]
- In the later window, A14, A15 and A20 appear regularly — A14 in about 29 of 100 traces (58 of 200), A15 in about 41 (82 of 200) and A20 in about 30 (59 of 200) — and no trace contains more than one of them; about 995 in 1000 later traces contain exactly one. [POS001, POS002, POS003, REL001, REL002, REL006]
- The new activities run inside the old fragment: A22 precedes the new activity in every trace containing both, the new activity precedes A24 in every trace containing both, and between the new activity and A23 there is no fixed order (for A15, about 57 of 100 joint traces have A15 before A23 and about 43 after it). [REL003, REL005, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]
- Direct successors shifted accordingly: A22 now leads to A23 in only about 44 of 100 of its observed outgoing transitions (previously all), with about 24 going to A15, 17 to A20 and 16 to A14; A23 now leads directly to A24 in about 57 of 100 (previously all), otherwise to one of the new activities. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Spacing shifted accordingly: A23 immediately follows A22 in 44 of 100 later traces (one event between them in 56, previously none), A24 immediately follows A23 in about 57 of 100 (previously all), and A24 now sits three events after A22 in about 995 of 1000 traces (previously exactly two; about 1 in 200 later traces still shows two). [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
- All three new activities appear around the middle of the trace (mean relative position about 0.51 with a tight spread), and A22's mean relative position moved slightly earlier, from about 0.48 to about 0.46, consistent with one extra event after it. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the previously fixed sequence A22 → A23 → A24 now contains an additional step: in the later window, one of three previously unobserved activities — A14, A15 or A20 — executes in almost every trace, placed between A22 and A23 in about 56 of 100 traces and between A23 and A24 in about 44, with A15 the most frequent choice (about 41 of 100 traces) and A14 and A20 at about 29–30 each. A22, A23 and A24 still occur in every trace in both windows; what changed is what runs between them. [REL003, REL004, REL005, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, DIR004, DIR005]

The hypothesis rests on direct relational evidence, not on frequency shifts alone: the order relations are observed outright (A22 always before the new activity, the new activity always before A24, both orders against A23), and the lag distributions between A22, A23 and A24 shifted by exactly the one event these placements imply. The screening comparison also rules out chance as an explanation for the ensemble: 24 control-flow items qualified where about 0.26 would be expected without a change — roughly 90 times the chance expectation — and every item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1000 random re-splits of the pooled data. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

Limitations: zero participation in the earlier window shows only that A14, A15 and A20 were not observed then, not that they could not occur, and the evidence cannot show whether the choice among the three activities, or their placement before versus after A23, follows a rule. An important competing explanation that cannot be fully excluded is that these activities already existed earlier at rates too low to appear in a 200-trace sample; the screening comparison shows the differences are too large for sampling noise overall, but it cannot rule out such a very rare earlier occurrence. [POS001, POS002, POS003, REL001, REL002, REL006, LAG002]
